paper_metadata.title: Creep Behavior and Damage of Ni-Base Superalloys PM 1000 and PM 3030

evidence.quote: Two oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS) nickel-base superalloys, a solely dispersion-strengthened alloy (PM 1000) and an additionally c¢-strengthened alloy (PM 3030) are investigated regarding creep resistance at temperatures between 600 /C176 C and 1000 /C176 C.

A serious drawback of the strengthening via c¢ precipitates is their thermal instability, which makes them more suitable for the intermediate temperature range rather than for temperatures significantly beyond 1000 /C176 C. At these high temperatures, oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS) is known to provide the best resistance to creep due to the excellent thermal stability of oxide dispersoids.
The creep strength advantage of PM 3030 over PM 1000 decreases as the temperature increases due to the thermal instability of the c¢ phase.
However, solid solution softening leads to an apparent drop in particle strengthening in PM 1000.

At 1000 /C176 C, however, the isotropic and fine-grained variant R901315 is inferior to R34 due to the increasing participation of grain boundary deformation processes in the overall creep deformation.

At low temperature (600 /C176 C), the creep resistance of both batches of PM 3030 is higher than that of PM 1000 in the entire investigated strain rate range due to additional c¢ precipitation strengthening.

At 1000 /C176 C, however, the isotropic and fine-grained variant R901315 is inferior to R34 due to the increasing participation of grain boundary deformation processes in the overall creep deformation.
However, solid solution softening leads to an apparent drop in particle strengthening in PM 1000.
